key_text_or_event: Mesopotamian grain accounting and shekel weight standards (c. 3000 BCE)
notes: Pre-literate or proto-literate era. Most records are clay tablets and oral transmission. High D due to geographic isolation and agricultural constraint.

dominant_paradigm: Coin-based market economies with commercial law
primary_transformation: Adoption of coinage and Roman commercial law
key_text_or_event: Lydian coinage (c. 600 BCE); Aristotle Politics (350 BCE); Roman commercial law
notes: First systematic thought on exchange and value. Aristotle distinguishes use value from exchange value. Roman law formalizes contract and debt.

dominant_paradigm: Feudal economy with emerging long-distance credit
paradigm_state: Ledger credit and bill of exchange
key_text_or_event: Pacioli Summa (1494); Medici Bank (1397); Champagne trade fairs
notes: Usury prohibition shapes credit instrument design. Bill of exchange circumvents interest ban. Deposit banking emerges in Italian city-states.

dominant_paradigm: Bullion accumulation doctrine and state-managed trade
primary_transformation: Joint-stock companies and national debt instruments
key_text_or_event: VOC incorporation (1602); Bank of England (1694); mercantilist treatises
notes: Trade surplus as state objective. Colonial systems extract bullion. National debt as war finance instrument. First rudimentary balance-of-trade statistics.

primary_transformation: Mathematical formalization and marginal utility analysis
key_text_or_event: Wealth of Nations (1776); Ricardo Principles (1817); Mill Principles (1848)
notes: Labor theory of value dominant. Free trade advocacy displaces mercantilism. Political economy becomes an academic discipline. First economic journals.

primary_transformation: Great Depression - model fails to explain persistent unemployment
key_text_or_event: Jevons Theory of Political Economy (1871); Walras Elements (1874); Marshall Principles (1890)
notes: Mathematics enters economics. Marginal utility replaces labor theory of value. Supply-demand equilibrium. Pareto optimum. First PhD programs in economics.

dominant_paradigm: Aggregate demand management and fiscal stabilization
primary_transformation: Stagflation - simultaneous inflation and unemployment invalidates IS-LM
key_text_or_event: General Theory (1936); Bretton Woods (1944); Kuznets national income accounting
notes: Depression reveals Say's Law failure. Fiscal multiplier. National income accounting created. Bretton Woods establishes IMF and World Bank. Mixed economy becomes policy norm.

dominant_paradigm: Price stability and quantity theory of money
key_text_or_event: Friedman monetarism; Lucas critique (1976); Volcker shock (1979-82)
notes: Stagflation discredits Keynesian discretion. Rational expectations. Rules vs discretion debate. Volcker disinflation. Reagan and Thatcher supply-side programs.

primary_transformation: Global Financial Crisis 2008 - efficient market consensus collapses
key_text_or_event: Washington Consensus (1989); WTO (1995); DSGE models; CDO expansion
custodian_class: IMF World Bank and economic policy institutes
notes: Capital account liberalization. DSGE macro models. Financial engineering and derivatives. Emerging market crises. Dot-com and housing bubbles as stress signals.

primary_transformation: Pending - no child N has yet stabilized
key_text_or_event: GFC (2008); Piketty Capital (2014); COVID-19 fiscal response (2020); LLM economics
notes: Models failed to predict 2008. Zero lower bound. Inequality debate. MMT. Complexity economics. Behavioral mainstream. AI in economics. No agreed successor paradigm.
